product_from_film: Wabi is a phone app for making, sharing and discovering small personal apps from ideas.
explains_well: The side-quest prompt leads to a named tracker and a phone task view, giving the mini-app idea a concrete example.
unclear: The film shows sharing choices and app examples but does not follow one friend joining and updating the shared tracker.
scenario: A rapid collage explains mini-apps, privacy choices, phone creation and several personal uses.
product_clear_basis: The coherent ASR draft says users can build apps inside the app at 6s; visible examples and the mini-app label follow.

sound.detail: The coherent ASR draft explains apps inside an app, sharing/privacy, no coding, phone creation, side quests, relationship analysis, goal cards and discovery. Minor words such as mini-app are mistranscribed. No voice delivery, music, effects or sync was heard or verified.
sound.visual_relation: V01–V07; draft supplies the connective explanation across the collage.

categories.finding: Question → mini-app definition → sharing and phone creation → examples → discovery → brand.
Analog hardware and What is wabi? create a direct question with a retro visual wrapper.
People wanting personal tools on their phones are the audience; side quests and goal cards make this specific.
App card groups, changing toggle states, a typed prompt and progress states provide movement cues; exact animation mechanics are unverified.
Reaction clips and title cards punctuate UI examples. Returning to the app grid reinforces the collection idea.
Mostly black/white typography surrounds colorful mini-app cards, analog hardware and mixed footage.
Large mini-app and personality words are easy to spot; dense relationship-analysis paragraphs are less readable at montage pace.
ASR gives a coherent informal explanation and repeated mini-app examples. Voice performance is unverified.
Music character and structure are unverified.
Effects and their sources are unverified.
categories.reason: No validated listening; waveform peaks do not identify effects.

categories.reason: No validated listening or paired audiovisual timing.

categories.finding: Analog equipment, recognizable film-like excerpts, phone footage, UI and retro computer graphics form a collage. Asset sources and rights are not checked.
Source duration 56.431 s; Watch metadata 1920 × 1080. Frame rate, audio clipping and export quality not checked here.

categories.finding: A phone prompt followed by a tracker makes the creation idea visible. The draft explains the relationship between many short clips.
Large labels, an arrow to the app icon and close phone controls guide attention.
Many short examples fit into 56s; the side-quest flow receives only about 5s.
The side-quest request becomes a named tracker and task screen, while discovery answers the no-idea problem.
Reaction footage and retro UI suggest playfulness; actual viewer emotion and sound character are unknown.
Personal goals and friend activities connect the product to small everyday needs.
Infinite creation, privacy behavior and report quality are film claims. A relationship score is an illustrated output, not a verified assessment.
The mixture of mini-app library, private/public choices and phone-made personal tools differentiates the story.
Complete the shared side-quest example.
